702580.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷatiléus, with σ (s) developing by assibilation. Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀣𐀯𐀩𐀄 (qa-si-re-u), that is, *gʷasileus.

702528.t: Onomatopoeic, from the perceived βαρ-βαρ (bar-bar) sounds incomprehensible to Ancient Greeks and spoken by foreigners.

702517.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷápt͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷh₂bʰ-yé-ti, from *gʷeh₂bʰ- (“to dive, dive in”).

702577.t: From the stem of βασιλεύς (basileús, “king”) + -ία (-íā, abstract noun suffix).

702566.t: From βάσανος (básanos, “touchstone”) + -ίζω (-ízō, “verbal suffix”), literally “to test with touchstone”.

702585.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷə́tis, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷémtis, from the root *gʷem- (“step”). By surface analysis, βαίνω (baínō, “to walk, step”) + -σις (-sĭs, nominal suffix).

702554.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷarus, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷréh₂us. Cognate to Sanskrit गुरु (gurú), Latin gravis.

702599.t: Seemingly imitative of croaking, with original form something like *βρατ-αχ- (*brat-akh-), but this imitation was probably not formed in Greek, but borrowed from Pre-Greek or Semitic; compare Hebrew צְפַרְדֵּעַ (ṣəp̄ardḗaʿ), Arabic ضَفْدَع (ḍafdaʕ),…

702521.t: Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *gʷerh₃- (“to devour”). Compare Latin vorāgō.

702598.t: Said by Beekes to be a Mediterranean wanderwort; substrate common to μαντία (mantía, “blackberry”) (Dacian loan), and Albanian man (“mulberry”), Gheg mand.

702589.t: Connected with βάσκειν (báskein, “to slander”), which is probably from βάζω (bázō, “to speak, say”), but might be related to Latin fascinum (“witchcraft; penis”), in which case both would derive from a European substrate language.

702594.t: Probably Pre-Greek. Has been compared to βαίνω (baínō, “to go, move”), but Beekes finds this unconvincing.

702570.t: From Egyptian bḫn (“a hard stone”), b-x:n-O39 via Lydia, which was used by the Egyptians as a touchstone of gold.

702593.t: From βαστάζω (bastázō, “I lift up, I raise”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).
